'''Raphaël Cerf''' is a French [[mathematician]] at [[Paris-Saclay University]] (previously [[Paris-Sud 11 University]]). For his contributions to [[probability theory]], he won the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] in 1999, and the [[EMS Prize]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RBanCdPm0ZIC&dq=Alesker%20EMS%20Prize&pg=PR24 |title=European Congress of Mathematics: Barcelona, July 10-14, 2000 |first=Carlos |last=Casacuberta |year=2001 |publisher=Birkhäuser |isbn=9783764364175 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200009/people.pdf|access-date=28 April 2023|title=Mathematics people|website=ams.org|date=October 2000}}</ref> He was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 2006 in Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icm2006.org/proceedings/vol3.html|title=Proceedings Volume III. Invited lectures|access-date=2 April 2018|archive-date=7 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307175915/http://www.icm2006.org/proceedings/vol3.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Selected works==
* {{cite web|url=http://images.math.cnrs.fr/Le-modele-d-Ising-et-la.html|title = Le modèle d'Ising et la coexistence des phases |author=Raphaël Cerf | website = images.math.cnrs.fr|date=15 October 2004}}
* ''The Wulff Crystal in Ising and Percolation models.'' Springer, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1878, École d’été de probabilités de Saint-Flour, no. 34, 2004
* ''On Cramér's Theory in infinite dimensions.'' Société Mathématique de France, 2007
* ''Large deviations for three dimensional supercritical percolation.'' Société Mathématique de France, 2000
